title: Recover the shared TR-6S/TR-8S firmware key (64-bit block cipher) via NOR bootloader dump
description:
The TR-6S and TR-8S App1_Main images are ECB-encrypted under a SHARED 64-bit block-cipher key (proven: 66,233 identical ciphertext blocks across the two images). Recovering the key once decrypts BOTH product lines. The key + decrypt routine live in the bootloader in NOR flash (Infineon S29GL512S on TR-6S), not in any shipped update file.

Because the key is shared, the hardware dump can target EITHER a TR-6S or a TR-8S -- whichever is easier to access. Steps: (1) locate JTAG/SWD/UART debug pads or the parallel-NOR bus; (2) dump the NOR; (3) find the bootloader's decrypt routine, identify the cipher (DES/3DES/Blowfish/XTEA/CAST/custom Feistel) and extract the key; (4) validate by decrypting App1_Main and checking the 0x50 header checksum over the plaintext.

Leverage: any plaintext from one unit is a known-plaintext oracle for the 66k shared blocks of the other. Gated behind hardware access (phase gate: read-only until recovery/DFU path confirmed).
notes:
SoC IDENTIFIED: the TR-6S/TR-8S main chip is Roland BMC (not E4E). TR-8S teardown photo shows 'Roland BMC' BGA, lot 5100440716. TR-6S shares the key with TR-8S => TR-6S is BMC too (strong inference via key-sharing sibling). E4E is a DIFFERENT chip = the AIRA Compact/T-8 SoC, which is why the T-8 firmware uses a different key. Key recovery target = the BMC bootloader in the TR-6S/TR-8S NOR.
Prior-art survey done (docs/prior-art.md): NO public JTAG/SWD/UART or firmware-decrypt exists for the Roland ACB/ZEN-Core platform (TR-8S/6S, MC-707/101, Fantom, Jupiter-X). Community RE is protocol-layer only. => hardware path is UNMAPPED, original RE, not a documented procedure. 'No writeup' != 'locked'; debug port could be open, untested. Cheap non-destructive route (find UART/SWD, attach, halt, read NOR@0x60000000) should be tried before chip-off. First-party recon checklist for the TR-6S is in the doc.
KEY SIZE: UNKNOWN. Block size = 64-bit is confirmed, but that is NOT the key size; key size is a property of the unidentified cipher (DES 56 / 3DES 112-168 / XTEA 128 / CAST 128 / IDEA 128 / Blowfish up to 448) and is only knowable from the decrypt routine (NOR dump). BRUTE-FORCE: only single DES (56-bit) is feasible (~1 day, ~$100 via crack.sh); >=112-bit is impossible (2^128). ECB weakness leaks structure, not the key. DES long-shot: fill block 6B4C9A85 2C732831 = E(K, padding) is a likely known-plaintext pair; IF DES, feed to crack.sh -> key. Rides on 2 assumptions (that it's DES + padding value). Fallback-to-a-fallback; the NOR dump reads the key directly regardless of size. Full writeup in docs/firmware-format.md 'Key size & brute-force feasibility'.
AIRA Compact trio added (J-6 DD011, E-4 DD012 alongside T-8 DD010). Confirms TWO disjoint key families tracking SoC: (1) TR/BMC key = TR-6S+TR-8S (our target); (2) AIRA-Compact/E4E key = T-8+J-6+E-4 (share 877-1870 blocks among themselves, 0 with the TRs). Recovering EITHER key unlocks that whole family. If the Compact/E4E hardware is ever easier to dump than a TR, its key decrypts 3 units — but it's a DIFFERENT key from the TR target.
SOFTWARE READ PATH lead: TR Editor implements Roland RQ1/DT1 SysEx (FKoaSendRq1/SendDt1/RequestRq1Dt1). RQ1 = read primitive over USB. Decompiling it yields the device address map -> potential NO-HARDWARE read of device memory (bypasses NOR chip-off if the address space reaches far enough). Binary imported to Ghidra as TREditor_x86_64.

title: tr-studio: ergonomic high-level API over tr-format (step grids, builders)
description: A library-manager CLI (later maybe TUI) built on tr-format: organize/dedupe/browse kits & patterns, batch-edit, import/export to JSON/TOML, and lay out an SD-card structure the TR-6S accepts. File-based only -- never writes to the device. The FOSS alternative to Roland Cloud bloatware. Depends on tr-format.
notes: tr-studio v0 SHIPPED: StepGrid (read/edit/render), voice mapping (tracks 0-5 = BD/SD/LT/HC/CH/OH, verified musically), pattern_grid() helper, 'tr-studio grid <backup> <ptn> [var]' CLI. Renders real beats from the backup (Speak C0DE: kick+backbeat snare+3-per-beat hats). In-memory edit via set/toggle/apply; write-back caveat: per-record checksum (+0x08) not recomputed yet, so not device-safe. tr-format got raw_mut() + Pattern::set_step_velocity() low-level writers. 2 tests. NEXT: track->inst for tracks 11-24 (sub-steps/motion), pattern builder ergonomics, and cracking the record checksum for device-safe writes.

title: tr-format: FOSS Rust library for TR-6S/8S user-data formats
description:
A Rust library to read/write/edit the TR-6S/TR-8S plaintext user-data formats: kits (.t6k), patterns (.t6p), backups (+ manifest), and sample references (WAV/AIFF). 100% plaintext user data -- NO firmware, NO decryption, no Roland IP (user's own content). Interoperability goal: a proper FOSS alternative to Roland's TR-EDITOR / Roland Cloud.

Design principles:
- BYTE-EXACT LOSSLESS ROUND-TRIP is the #1 requirement: parse(bytes).to_bytes() == bytes, guaranteed by property tests. A librarian must never corrupt unknown/reserved fields, so keep a typed view over known fields + preserve all unknown bytes verbatim.
- Typed model per format (Kit/Pattern/Backup/SampleRef) with raw passthrough for not-yet-understood regions.
- read/write/edit API; validate any internal checksums (the .t6k/.t6p may carry their own, like the firmware CRC-32 -- TBD).
- Optional serde layer: binary <-> typed <-> JSON/TOML so kits/patterns become human-editable and diffable.

RE-driven workflow: (1) obtain real files, (2) reverse the format with fw-analyze hexdump + the new block/byte diff (save two kits differing by ONE parameter -> diff locates that field), (3) implement parsers incrementally with byte-exact round-trip tests. Fixtures: keep REAL user/factory files gitignored (factory content may be Roland IP); commit synthetic/minimized fixtures only.

Blocked on: sample files from a device backup.
notes:
v0 SHIPPED: tr-format crate parses the TR-6S backup container (TR6S magic + 16-byte tagged chunks: SYS/PTN/KIT/SMPL/FX), lists sections with array shapes, and guarantees BYTE-EXACT round-trip (verified on the real 54MB backup). Section map RE'd: PTN=128 records x 24504B, KIT=128 x 1312B (6 voices BD/SD/LT/HC/CH/OH), SYS reuses init_param body. Manifest (*_bak.txt) = labeled ground truth (128 patterns/kits w/ names+tempo+kit refs). Spec: docs/tr-format.md. NEXT: decode kit record (1312B, smallest) then pattern record via diff-two-and-compare.
Kit record decoded (framing + name): 128 records x 0x520B in KIT section, name at +0x10 [16]. tr-format now has Kit/kits() + 'tr-format kits' CLI — lists all 128, verified vs manifest. Findings: +0x00 [16] per-record header w/ unidentified 8B checksum at +0x08 (not plain CRC-32; needed for WRITE); voices reference tone IDs into a separate 144B-entry tone table ~0x326fd4. NEXT: locate 6 tone-ID fields + per-voice params via controlled one-change diffs.
Voices decoded (tentative, TDD'd, TODO-labeled): TONE section @0x326f90, 0x24-byte entries (name[16]+params[20]). Kit voice tone-IDs = u16 LE at record+0x194+voice*0x34 (BD/SD/LT/HC/CH/OH). Cross-checked kits 0-3 -> all resolve correctly (808/909/707/727). tr-format: Kit::voice_tone_ids, Backup::tone_name, 'tr-format kit <n>' CLI (resolves voices to tone names on the real backup). 10 tests. Marked TODO(controlled-diff): the rest of each 0x34 voice block + write-checksum still need save-change-save confirmation.
TR EDITOR = ORACLE. It's a JUCE C++ app (universal x86_64+arm64, symbols intact), imported to Ghidra (TREditor_x86_64). Full param tree recovered from strings: fm.usrKit[k].instCommon[i] = voice block; instToneValueRef = confirmed +0x00 tone-ID. Instrument params: level, instOutput, instGroupCombo, instFilterValueRef, instCtrlKnob/Select (assignable CTRL, tone-dependent) — NO fixed pan/tune/decay (supersedes earlier guesses). Sections map 1:1: usrKit=KIT, usrPtn=PTN (ptnVar=variations, KIT REFFERENCE), tone=TONE, PCM_TONE=samples, SYS. NEXT: decompile the backup serializer/param table for definitive name->offset mapping.
TR Editor Ghidra analysis COMPLETE (15,442 functions). RE targets identified for name->offset mapping: CKoaValueRef @ 0x100344310 (per-param descriptor class — instToneValueRef etc. are instances; encodes param address/offset), UpdateValueRefs @ 0x1003df120, SendRolandRq1Message @ 0x100318d30 + CommandRq1 @ 0x100413bb0 (RQ1 SysEx builder -> device address map), CBackupper @ 0x100416810. NOTE: the BackUp() functions are google::protobuf (cloud/sync), NOT the device backup — the Roland 'CKoa*' layer is the right one. Addresses are from this import (Mach-O base 0x100000000). NEXT: decompile CKoaValueRef + SendRolandRq1Message to extract param->offset and confirm the voice-block field map.
VOICE BLOCK FULLY DECODED + CONFIRMED via TR Editor schema (Contents/Resources/Script/Script.xml, structType instCommon[0]). Every default matches observed bytes: TONE(u16,+0x00) TUNE(+0x02) DECAY(+0x03) LEVEL(+0x04) GAIN(+0x05) PAN(+0x06) REVERB_SEND(+0x07) DELAY_SEND(+0x08) LFO_SWITCH(+0x09) LFO_DEST(+0x0a) LFO_DEPTH(+0x0b) CATEGORY_LOCK(+0x0c). Corrects earlier stat guesses. tr-format: VoiceParams + Kit::voices(); 'tr-format kit <n>' shows named params on real backup. 12 tests. KEY: Script.xml is the data-driven schema oracle (27.8k lines, addresses match backup: kit=03,ptn=04) -> use it to decode patterns/FX/SYS next, no controlled diff needed.
PATTERN HEADER decoded via Script.xml ptnCmn + verified vs manifest (all 128 patterns' name/tempo/kit match). Offsets: name +0x10[16], TEMPO +0x20 (u16 BPMx10), KIT REFFERENCE +0x22 (u8). tr-format: Pattern + patterns(); 'tr-format patterns' lists name/tempo/kit. Schema rule confirmed: intNxM = ceil(N*M/8) bytes. 13 tests. NEXT: reconcile ~1-byte offset drift past header, then decode ptnVar* step/motion (the builder core: variations A-H, 6 insts x 16 steps as int8x4 words). FX/SYS decode identically from Script.xml.
OFFSET MODEL SOLVED. Rule: record_offset = 0x0F + schema_offset; sizes int1x7/int2x4=1, int2x7=2, int8x4=4, stringNx7=16, int4x4=ceil(bits(range_max)/7) [the missing piece: 16-bit masks like SHUFFLE SWITCH=3 bytes, TONE/TEMPO=2]. Validated 102/103 ptnCmn fields in range. Encoded as schema_value_size(). Pattern body = ptnCmn + 10 variations (A-H+2 fills) x per-inst 16-step arrays; step word (int8x4)= byte0 velocity (0=off). Verified var A INST01 of 'Speak C0DE' reads a real beat at record+0xA0. StepWord type added. 15 tests. NEXT: per-variation/inst stride -> step grid read/write API -> pattern builder. FX/SYS same method.
PATTERN STRIDE NAILED (empirical): variation A @ record+0xA0, stride 0x984 (2436B) [accent 4 + 25 step-arrays x64 + motion 832]. step_word_offset = 0xA0 + var*0x984 + 4 + track*64 + step*4. Verified reads real beats. Low-level added to tr-format: PATTERN_* stride consts + Pattern::step_word/step_word_offset (raw, no ergonomics). 16 tests. ARCH: keep tr-format low-level (offsets/records/StepWord); step-grid + pattern-builder ergonomics go in a higher-level crate (cowbell-6gm). track->instrument mapping is higher-level.

title: fw-analyze diff: block-aligned ECB comparison (--block/--offset)
description: Add block-aligned diff to fw-analyze for comparing encrypted ECB images across products/revisions: per-image duplicate-block ratio (ECB signature), set-based overlap, positional same-offset overlap, and longest identical run in original-file coords. Validated: reproduces the manual TR-6S/TR-8S analysis exactly (29.89% dup, 66233 shared, 15936-byte run at 0x252fb8).
close_reason: Implemented and validated against real images; commit incoming

title: Reverse-engineer T-8 App_Panel (plaintext ARM) to learn Roland conventions
description: T-8 App_Panel is plaintext ARM Cortex-M, already imported to the Ghidra project (DD010_pnl_ARM.bin, base 0x08000000, 196 functions). Free desk work, no hardware. Goals: (1) identify the header CHECKSUM routine -- the 0x50 field appears in every image's header; if the panel image validates its own body with a known algorithm we may crack the checksum used across the encrypted images too. (2) Map peripheral usage (which STM32 peripherals, matrix scan for the 74HC138) to confirm the exact STM32G0 variant and pin map. (3) Establish Roland's compiler/toolchain fingerprint (libc stub, SystemInit) for cross-referencing the eventual decrypted E4E code. Related: cowbell-hu6.
notes: CHECKSUM RESOLVED (computationally, via known-plaintext — no ARM reversing needed). The header checksum (0x50 for App1_Main, 0x2c for compact App* layout) is STANDARD CRC-32 (zlib crc32, poly 0x04C11DB7, reflected, init/xorout 0xFFFFFFFF) over the image body. Proven: CRC-32 of the plaintext App_Panel body == its 0x53c790fb field exactly. Also proven the CRC is over PLAINTEXT: CRC-32 over the ciphertext of the encrypted images matches nothing (TR-6S 0x25f6cee3 != 0x46de65b3). => bootloader decrypts THEN CRCs. Bonus: this is a decryption ORACLE for cowbell-8o5 — correct key is the one whose decrypted-body CRC-32 == header field.
close_reason: App_Panel RE done in Ghidra: toolchain = STM32Cube HAL + GCC/newlib; peripheral map from IRQ table (USART1/ADC+DMA/EXTI/TIM1,3,14, no SPI); panel<->BMC protocol = MIDI-over-UART (Note On/Off ch0/1/3, Active Sensing keepalive, 3-byte packets, DMA ping-pong TX). Documented in firmware-format.md; functions renamed + plate-commented in the Ghidra DB.

title: fw-extract: recognise and unwrap tar update containers
description:
TR6S_UP.bin (Roland TR-6S sys v2.00) is a GNU tar archive, not a raw firmware image — 'fw-extract identify' currently only knows exe/msi/dmg/pkg containers and misses it entirely. The archive holds two members under ./_tmp/: dd001_m0c0a_up.bin (2529328 B, encrypted App1_Main image) and dd001_init_param.bin (1376256 B, plaintext INIT param blob).

Scope:
- identify: detect tar (GNU/ustar magic 'ustar' at offset 0x101, plus the header-name/checksum sanity check) and report it as a container type.
- unpack: extract tar members natively (or shell to 'tar' consistent with the existing 7z/msiextract/xar delegation pattern), stripping the ./_tmp/ prefix.
- carve: rank the extracted members. Should surface dd001_m0c0a_up.bin as the dense/encrypted payload (entropy ~7.98) and flag dd001_init_param.bin as lower-entropy data.

Acceptance:
- 'fw-extract identify TR6S_UP.bin' prints tar (not 'unknown').
- 'fw-extract unpack' yields both members on disk.
- unit test with a small synthetic tar fixture (no Roland bytes committed).

Ref: docs/firmware-format.md 'Container — RESOLVED' section.
close_reason: Implemented native tar detect+unpack; validated on real TR6S/TR8S/T8 update files (byte-identical extraction, path-safe, prefix-stripped). 6 tests pass.

title: Characterize E4E via AIRA Compact Beat 8 reference platform
description:
The TR-6S main audio SoC is (candidate) a Roland E4E. The AIRA Compact 'Beat 8' shares a CONFIRMED Roland E4E (BGA, marked 'Roland E4E', lot 5100069694, date 2304) and is cheap, openable, firmware-downloadable, and already open on the bench. Use it as the reference platform to crack the E4E without a TR-6S teardown.

Context confirmed from board photos (2026-08-07):
- Beat 8 audio SoC = Roland E4E (discrete silicon, not marketing).
- Beat 8 panel MCU = ST STM32G0 (ARM Cortex-M0+, LQFP48) + 74HC138 matrix decoder.
- 8-pin SOIC marked 251/P2368 sits beside the E4E -- candidate external SPI NOR/EEPROM.
- App1_Main image load addr = 0x60000000 (ARM external-NOR-bank base) -> ARM ISA hypothesis for E4E.

Sub-tasks:
1. Download Roland's Beat 8 / AIRA Compact firmware update(s). Run through fw-extract/fw-analyze: is the container the same tar+App-header format? Is the payload ECB-encrypted like the TR-6S, or plaintext? Same 64-bit block cipher? Does the checksum algorithm reveal itself on a plaintext image?
2. Identify the 251/P2368 SOIC-8 (match marking to a datasheet). If SPI NOR: in-circuit SOIC-8 clip dump (CH341A/flashrom, no soldering) -> first look at real E4E-adjacent code/data.
3. If plaintext E4E code is obtained, confirm ISA (ARM vs other) and pick the Ghidra language spec. This retro-answers the TR-6S ISA question IF the two units share the E4E.

Acceptance: either (a) a decrypted/plaintext code region attributable to the E4E, or (b) a definitive ISA identification, whichever comes first. Feeds docs/hardware.md and architecture-questions.md.

Blocks: any TR-6S bootloader/decryption work. Cheaper and faster than the S29GL512S chip-off on the TR-6S.
notes:
CORRECTION: the Beat 8 board photos are third-party (Reddit), NOT the maintainer's hardware. We do NOT have a Beat 8 on hand. Split this bead by cost: (1) FREE/NOW = download Roland Beat 8 / AIRA Compact firmware and analyze container+encryption vs TR-6S (no hardware needed); (2) BLOCKED-ON-PURCHASE = the SOIC-8 clip-dump and any board probing require acquiring a unit first. The E4E-is-real-silicon and STM32G0 findings still stand as external corroboration.
FIRMWARE COMPARISON DONE (free half). Analyzed T8_UPD.BIN (T-8/Beat 8 v1.02) + TR8S_UP.bin (TR-8S v3.00) alongside TR6S. Results: (1) Container = same Roland tar+App-header format across all 3. (2) T-8 App_Main encrypted with a DIFFERENT key (0 shared blocks) -> NOT a key shortcut. (3) T-8 App_Panel is PLAINTEXT ARM Cortex-M -> imported to Ghidra, 196 functions, confirms panel-MCU ISA. (4) BONUS: TR-6S and TR-8S SHARE the encryption key (66,233 identical ciphertext blocks). The remaining hardware sub-task (SPI dump of E4E-adjacent flash) still needs a purchased unit and is lower priority now that ISA is confirmed via the panel image.
REFRAME: E4E (Beat 8) is NOT the TR-6S chip. TR-6S main SoC = BMC (confirmed on TR-8S sibling). E4E is a separate AIRA-Compact part with its own key. So the Beat 8 is only a generic ARM/toolchain reference, not representative of TR-6S silicon -- lowers its value. Deprioritize acquiring a Beat 8.
